context:
Goal: the merge tool never repeats an act on GitHub that may already have happened, such as a merge or a posted comment.
Problem (rule): your ruling of Oct 16 keeps 3 retries on every GitHub call; the lane's fix sends a write (PUT, POST, PATCH, DELETE) once on a server error or lost reply, so it changes your ruling and the merge of PR #2964 waits for your word.
Based on (measured): on this PR's head the merge PUT goes out once; on main it goes out 4 times (lane retry-net-method-safe, 15:19 CST today).
Based on (read): the 3 retries protected a merge run from failing on one lost reply; now, after one lost reply, the merge reads the PR's state: merged carries on, still open stops with "run again".
Departs from: main retries every GitHub call 3 times on a server error — a write is sent once and the merge reads the PR's state; reads and rate limits still retry 3 times.
home: decision standing-merge-grant (its sentence on the 3 retries)

options.gain: A write the server may already have done is never sent again, so no double merge or double comment.
options.how: The lane keeps its change; the decision's sentence becomes "A non-idempotent method is sent once on a 5xx or network error", with your time.
options.label: Send a write once (Recommended)
options.lose: One more run to type when a write's reply is lost and the PR is still open.

options.gain: A lost reply on a write is retried with no run to repeat.
options.how: The lane drops the change for writes; your Oct 16 ruling stands as written.
options.label: Keep 3 retries for every call
options.lose: A write the server already did can be sent up to 3 more times, as the merge PUT is today.

short: Writes sent once on a server error
title: May the merge tool send a write to GitHub only once on a server error?
why: The fix changes your Oct 16 ruling of 3 retries for every call.
